---
title: "Spatial analysis in primary tumor samples"
author: "LazDaria"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: 
  workflowr::wflow_html
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: inline
params:
  input: !r Sys.getenv("MAPMET_INPUT", "/mnt/data/input_all")
  output: !r Sys.getenv("MAPMET_OUTPUT", "/mnt/data/output")

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Plots directory
plot_dir <- file.path(params$output, "plots/07_spatial_analysis")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) {
  dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}


# Date prefix for filenames
date_prefix <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d")

# Save a plot (ggplot / ComplexHeatmap / base) into a figure subfolder
save_plot <- function(plot_obj, filename, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300, subdir = NULL) {
  # Unless a subfolder is given (cell_counts, density_analysis),
  # route every figure into exactly one of three subfolders by filename:
  # cell-cell_interaction (Fig4b), neighborhood_level (anything CN/neighborhood-
  # related, incl. the combined Fig4d stack), celltype_level (everything else -
  # tumor/immune celltype breakdowns, spatial compartments, border distance by
  # celltype).
  if (is.null(subdir))
    subdir <- if (grepl("cell-cell_interactions", filename))               "cell-cell_interaction" else
              if (grepl("neighborhood|Fig4d_combined_stacked", filename))  "neighborhood_level"    else
                                                                            "celltype_level"
  out_dir   <- file.path(plot_dir, subdir)
  if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  full_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(date_prefix, "_", filename))

  if (inherits(plot_obj, "ggplot")) {
    
    ggsave(full_path, plot = plot_obj, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi)
    
  } else if (inherits(plot_obj, c("Heatmap", "HeatmapList", "HeatmapAnnotation"))) {
    
    pdf(full_path, width = width, height = height)
    draw(plot_obj)
    dev.off()
    
  } else {
    
    dev.copy(pdf, full_path, width = width, height = height)
    dev.off()
  }
  
  message("Saved: ", full_path)
}

# Tables directory, with the same subfolders as the plots
table_dir <- file.path(params$output, "tables/07_spatial_analysis")

# Save a table as csv into a subfolder of table_dir
save_table <- function(df, filename, subdir) {
  out_dir <- file.path(table_dir, subdir)
  if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  full_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(date_prefix, "_", filename))
  write.csv(df, full_path, row.names = FALSE)
  message("Saved: ", full_path)
}

# Global chunk options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  dev = "png",
  dpi = 300,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 6
)
```

# Spatial analysis in PT {#sp-pt}

Herein, we explore spatial interactions in the primary tumor. 
Due to a [bug](https://github.com/BodenmillerGroup/imcRtools) in the `testInteractions` function in imcRtools versions < 1.5.5, we provide another docker image with a newer imcRtools version for spatial analysis. Please pull *lazdaria/mapmetsc_spatial:v1.0* from [docker hub]() and for the present RMD file.

## Load libraries
<details>
   <summary>Load libraries</summary>
   
```{r load-libraries}
library(imcRtools)
library(scales)
library(BiocParallel)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(circlize)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(lisaClust)
library(tidyr)
library(diffcyt)
library(dplyr)
library(CATALYST)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(gtools)
library(ggpubr)
library(gridExtra)
library(ggridges)
library(forcats)
library(pheatmap)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggdendro)
library(sf)
```
</details>

## Read data
First, we load the phenotyped single-cell data ([chapter 4](#phenotyping)) from the 05.1 checkpoint, which also carries the cellular-community (`tumor_community`) annotation. We perform spatial analysis only in the primary tumor samples, since the bone marrow samples are aspirates, where the spatial context is lost. Therefore, we first subset the SPE object to the PT samples and then load cell neighbors that were computed in [MapMetIP](https://github.com/TaschnerMandlGroup/MapMetIP). Therein, we have extracted neighbors by expanding individual high-resolution cell masks by 15 pixels. We load the cell neighbors for the primary-tumour samples directly with `read_steinbock`, using its `pattern` argument to select the `TU` samples from the shared `intensities-0px` folder (no file duplication needed).

```{r temp-folder}
# No temp folder / file duplication needed: read_steinbock() below selects the
# TU samples directly via its `pattern` argument.
```

We can now read in the neighbors.
For the spatial interaction analysis, we will use the metaclusters for non-tumor cells, since these represent the minority in the PT samples, and the celltype level annotations for the tumor cells (majority).

```{r read-data}
# Sample-annotation and structural colors (COL_CODE, COL_COMPARTMENT, COL_CN)
# from 00_MapMet_color_code.R - sourced early so they are available as soon as
# the corresponding columns are derived below / further down this file.
for (mapmet_cc_path in c("analysis/00_MapMet_color_code.R", "00_MapMet_color_code.R", "../analysis/00_MapMet_color_code.R"))
  if (file.exists(mapmet_cc_path)) { source(mapmet_cc_path); break }

# Load the phenotyped object from 05.1 (carries the tumor_community column used below)
spe <- readRDS(file.path(params$output,"spe_05.1_PT_DE_cellularcomm.rds"))
spe <- spe[,spe$tissue=="PT"]

spe_neighbors <- read_steinbock(path=file.path(params$input), image_file=NULL, panel_file = NULL, intensities_folder = "intensities-0px",regionprops_folder = NULL, graphs_folder="neighbors", pattern = "TU")
colnames(spe_neighbors) <- paste0(spe_neighbors$sample_id, "_", spe_neighbors$ObjectNumber)
colPair(spe, "neighborhood") <- colPair(spe_neighbors[,colnames(spe)], "neighborhood")

#celltype 2
spe$celltype_2 <- spe$metacluster
spe[,spe$metacluster=="tumor"]$celltype_2 <- spe[,spe$metacluster=="tumor"]$celltype

# generate new color vector
tumor_names <- unique(spe[,spe$metacluster=="tumor"]$celltype)
metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_2 <- metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_metacluster
metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_2 <- c(metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_2, metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype[tumor_names])

#celltype 3 (used below to count "immune" cells per compartment)
spe$celltype_3 <- spe$metacluster
spe[,spe$metacluster=="T cells" | spe$metacluster=="B cells" | spe$metacluster=="granulocytes" | spe$metacluster=="myeloid/NK"]$celltype_3 <- "immune"
```

## Interaction analysis

Next, we determine the interactions between cells on the metacluster level. For each image, the `testInteractions` function computes the averaged cell type interactions and compares this number against an empirical null distribution generated by permuting all cell labels, while maintaining tissue structure.

```{r interaction-analysis}
out <- testInteractions(spe,
                        group_by = "sample_id",
                        label = "metacluster",
                        colPairName = "neighborhood",
                        BPPARAM = SerialParam(RNGseed = 221029))
```

These interactions can be shown in a heatmap.

```{r interaction-heatmap, fig.width=5, fig.height=5}

data <- out %>% as_tibble() %>%
    group_by(from_label, to_label) %>%
    summarize(sum_sigval = sum(sigval, na.rm = TRUE))

data_wide <- data %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = to_label,
    values_from = sum_sigval
  )

data_wide <- tibble::column_to_rownames(data_wide, var = "from_label")

# Fixed symmetric color range (+/-50), so breaks are centred on 0
max_range <- max(abs(50), abs(50))
breaks <- seq(-max_range, max_range, length.out = 101)

# blue-white-red scale
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(length(breaks) - 1)

p_heatmap <- pheatmap(data_wide,
         color = colors,
         breaks = breaks,
         cellwidth = 20,
         cellheight = 20,
         fontsize = 10,
         display_numbers = TRUE,
         number_format = "%.0f")

save_plot(p_heatmap, "Fig4b_cell-cell_interactions.pdf", width = 6, height = 6)
```

## Cellular neighborhoods

In a next step, we detect cellular neighborhoods (CNs). For each cell, we compute the fraction of each cell type (celltype_2) among its neighbors, and then aggregate cells into a predefined number of neighborhoods (here 6) by k-means.

```{r c-neighborhoods cn-analysis, fig.width=20, fig.height=50}
spe <- aggregateNeighbors(spe, 
                          colPairName = "neighborhood", 
                          aggregate_by = "metadata", 
                          count_by = "celltype_2")

set.seed(220705)

n_neighborhoods <- 6

cn_1 <- kmeans(spe$aggregatedNeighbors, centers = n_neighborhoods)
spe$cn_celltypes_2 <- as.factor(cn_1$cluster)

# Centralized neighborhood palette (COL_CN, from 00_MapMet_color_code.R) so the
# same CN -> color mapping is reused everywhere below (and in 08_generate_images).
metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn <- COL_CN[levels(spe$cn_celltypes_2)]

p_spatial <- plotSpatial(spe,
            node_color_by = "cn_celltypes_2",
            img_id = "sample_id",
            ncols=6,
            node_size_fix = 0.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn)

save_plot(p_spatial, "Fig4f_spatial_neighborhood_images.pdf", width = 20, height = 49)

p_spatial
```

Lastly, we can visualize the enrichment of cell types within cellular neighborhoods
using the `regionMap` function of the `lisaClust` package.

```{r regionmap, fig.height=6, fig.width=5}
library(lisaClust)

# TEMP DEBUG (grep logs for "COL_CN_DEBUG"): verify col_cn is a valid, fully
# named 6-color vector right before plot_cn_region_map() uses it, to check
# whether an upstream issue (not the Fig4c plotting code itself) is behind
# the missing badge colors. Uses cat(..., file = stderr()) rather than
# message() so it is never swallowed by this doc's global message=FALSE
# chunk option and always reaches the render log.
cat("COL_CN_DEBUG region_levels:", paste(levels(spe$cn_celltypes_2), collapse = ", "), "\n", file = stderr())
cat("COL_CN_DEBUG col_cn names:", paste(names(metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn), collapse = ", "), "\n", file = stderr())
cat("COL_CN_DEBUG col_cn values:", paste(metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn, collapse = ", "), "\n", file = stderr())
cat("COL_CN_DEBUG col_cn length:", length(metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn), "\n", file = stderr())
cat("COL_CN_DEBUG col_cn class:", paste(class(metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn), collapse = ", "), "\n", file = stderr())

# Region map (cell-type enrichment per CN) for a given CN column of spe and its
# CN -> color vector.
plot_cn_region_map <- function(spe, region_col, col_regions) {
  p_map <- regionMap(spe,
            cellType = "celltype_2",
            region = region_col)

  p_map <- p_map + ggplot2::coord_flip() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

  # Replace the plain "1".."k" region-axis labels with colored badges (CN
  # color fill, black number, no border) drawn in a separate column next to
  # the heatmap, combined via patchwork. Built from plain geom_point()/
  # geom_text() layers (not annotation_custom + raw grid grobs, which need an
  # already-established coordinate system and are easy to get silently wrong
  # on an empty ggplot()) so the scale is trained normally like any other plot.
  # regionMap() maps `region` to the x aesthetic (aes(x = region, y = cellType,
  # ...) - see lisaClust's R/LISA.R); coord_flip() only changes where that
  # renders (here, the now-blanked y-axis). The badge column maps the same
  # region categories onto its own y axis, so it gets the identical default
  # discrete-scale layout regionMap() uses, and patchwork's panel-height
  # alignment lines its rows up with the heatmap's.
  p_map <- p_map + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
                          axis.title.y = element_blank())

  region_levels <- levels(spe[[region_col]])
  region_df <- data.frame(x = 1, region = factor(region_levels, levels = region_levels))

  p_region_labels <- ggplot2::ggplot(region_df, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = region)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(fill = region), shape = 21, size = 11, colour = NA) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = region), colour = "black", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = col_regions, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 1.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::labs(y = "Region") +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 90, size = 11),
                   plot.margin  = ggplot2::margin(0, 2, 0, 2))

  # TEMP DEBUG (grep logs for "COL_CN_DEBUG"): tell apart a scale/geom bug
  # (p_region_labels is colorless even on its own) from a patchwork
  # combination/rendering bug (p_region_labels is fine alone, but the colors
  # disappear once combined with p_map below) - save it standalone and log
  # the fill colour ggplot actually computed per point.
  cat("COL_CN_DEBUG p_region_labels computed fill (", region_col, "):",
      paste(ggplot2::layer_data(p_region_labels, 1)$fill, collapse = ", "), "\n", file = stderr())
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir, paste0(date_prefix, "_DEBUG_p_region_labels_", region_col, ".pdf")),
    plot = p_region_labels, width = 2, height = 4)

  (p_region_labels | p_map) + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 6))
}

# Final map, using the k = n_neighborhoods (6) CNs used for all other plots
p_map <- plot_cn_region_map(spe, "cn_celltypes_2", metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn)

save_plot(p_map, "Fig4c_spatial_neighborhood_map.pdf", width = 8.5, height = 4)

p_map
```

To check how robust the neighborhoods are to the choice of k, we also draw the
region map for k = 4 to 8. Each k re-runs k-means with the same seed as above
(so k = 6 reproduces the final CNs); these CNs are only used for these maps.

```{r regionmap-k-sweep, fig.height=6, fig.width=5}
# Set3 palette extended to 8 colors; its first 6 are COL_CN, so CN colors match
# the final k = 6 map.
col_cn_sweep <- setNames(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set3"), as.character(1:8))

for (k in 4:8) {
  set.seed(220705)
  cn_k <- kmeans(spe$aggregatedNeighbors, centers = k)
  spe$cn_k_sweep <- as.factor(cn_k$cluster)

  p_map_k <- plot_cn_region_map(spe, "cn_k_sweep",
                                col_cn_sweep[levels(spe$cn_k_sweep)])
  save_plot(p_map_k, paste0("Fig4c_spatial_neighborhood_map_k", k, ".pdf"),
            width = 8.5, height = 4)
  print(p_map_k)
}

# Drop the temporary column so only the final CNs (cn_celltypes_2) are kept
spe$cn_k_sweep <- NULL
```
         
### CN abundance per sample

Finally, we will generate a barplot showing the proportions of CNs per sample. To do so, we first transform the SPE object into a CATALYST-compatible SingleCellExperiment.

```{r transform-data, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays=list(counts=assay(spe, "counts"), exprs=assay(spe, "counts")))

#recode metadata on progression
sce$progress <- factor(spe$progression)
progress <- recode(sce$progress, `0` = 'NoProg', `1` = 'Prog')
sce$progress <- as.factor(progress)

#recode metadata on MYCN amplification
sce$mna <- factor(spe$MYCN_amp)
mna <- recode(sce$mna, `1` = 'MNA', `2` = 'het', `0` = 'nMNA', `9` = 'unknown')
sce$mna <- as.factor(mna)

sce$tumor_community <- factor(spe$tumor_community)

sce$patient <- factor(spe$patient_id)
sce$fm_id <- spe$fm_id

sce$sample_id <- factor(paste0(sce$progress, "_", sce$mna, "_", sce$patient, "_", sce$fm_id))

sce$cluster_id <- factor(spe$cn_celltypes_2)
sce$metacluster <- factor(spe$metacluster)

sce$condition <- 'na' 

# Add celltype information to metadata
metadata(sce)$cluster_codes <- data.frame(celltype = factor(spe$cn_celltypes_2))
```

Next, we will generate a barplot showing the proportion of cells assigned to each of the 6 CNs per sample.

```{r cohort-overview}
set.seed(20231103)

distance <- "manhattan"
linkage <- "complete"

p <- plotAbundances(sce, k = "celltype", by = "sample", col_clust=T, k_pal=metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn,
                    linkage = linkage, distance= distance)

save_plot(p, "Fig4d1_spatial_neighborhood_clustering.pdf", width = 6, height = 4)

p
```

We generate a dendogram for the hierarchical clustering of barplots.

```{r dendrogram, fig.height=8, fig.width=7}
set.seed(20231103)
wide_df <- p$data %>%
  select(-condition) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = cluster_id, values_from = Freq)

wide_df <- data.frame(wide_df)
rownames(wide_df) <- wide_df$sample_id
wide_df <- wide_df %>% select(-sample_id)

dist_matrix <- dist(wide_df, method = distance)
hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = linkage)

p2 <- plot(hc)

save_plot(p2, "Fig4d2_spatial_neighborhood_clustering_dendogram.pdf", width = 6, height = 6)
p2
```

In addition, we plot the metadata of these samples in the respective order.

```{r plot-metadata, fig.height=3}
clustered_samples <- levels(p$data$sample_id)
sce$sample_id <- factor(sce$sample_id, levels=clustered_samples)

#access sample-level data
sample_summary <- as.data.frame(colData(sce)) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarize(mna = first(mna), 
            progress=first(progress),
            tumor_community=first(tumor_community),
  )

sample_summary <- as.data.frame(sample_summary)
rownames(sample_summary) <- sample_summary$sample_id
sample_summary <- sample_summary %>% select(-sample_id)


# Sample-annotation colors (COL_CODE sourced from 00_MapMet_color_code.R in the
# read-data chunk above)
col_code <- COL_CODE

# Explicit patient-group palette (col_code's 1/2/3 = blue/red/green is used
# elsewhere); shared with the combined Fig4d strip below.
community_cols <- c("1" = "#E6C700", "2" = "#C71585", "3" = "#4DAF4A")


# Plot metadata
p_anno<- columnAnnotation(MYCN_amp=sample_summary$mna, col=list(MYCN_amp=col_code)) %v%
  columnAnnotation(progression=sample_summary$progress, col=list(progression=col_code)) %v%
  columnAnnotation(patient_group=as.character(sample_summary$tumor_community), col=list(patient_group=community_cols))

save_plot(p_anno, "Fig4d3_spatial_neighborhood_clustering_metadata.pdf", width = 8, height = 4)

p_anno
```

Finally, we assemble the dendrogram, the CN-abundance barplot and the three metadata strips into a single stacked figure (Fig4d).

```{r fig4d-combined-stacked, fig.height=8.4, fig.width=8}

ddata <- dendro_data(hc, type = "rectangle")
segs <- segment(ddata)

p_dendro <- ggplot(segs) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 0, 2)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Sample clustering based on cellular neighborhood composition")

meta_df <- sample_summary[clustered_samples, c("mna", "progress", "tumor_community")]
meta_df$sample_id <- factor(rownames(meta_df), levels = clustered_samples)

# One annotation strip per track, each with its own fill scale so the three
# legends render separately. patient_group uses the explicit community palette.
make_meta_strip <- function(df, ann_col, legend_title, cols) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = sample_id, y = 1, fill = as.character(.data[[ann_col]]))) +
    # explicit height (y is constant)
    geom_tile(height = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cols, na.value = "white", name = legend_title) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(y = legend_title) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 9),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 0, 2)
    )
}

p_meta_mna   <- make_meta_strip(meta_df, "mna",                   "MYCN_amp",      col_code)
p_meta_prog  <- make_meta_strip(meta_df, "progress",              "progression",   col_code)
p_meta_group <- make_meta_strip(meta_df, "tumor_community", "patient_group", community_cols)
# extra bottom margin so the last strip is not clipped
p_meta_group <- p_meta_group + theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 2, 2))

# Abundance barplot: rename the CN legend and drop the placeholder "na" facet
p_abund <- p +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn,
                    name = "Cellular neighborhood") +
  facet_null() +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 0, 2)
  )

# Relative panel heights: dendrogram / abundance / three metadata strips
panel_heights <- c(1.2, 4, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25)
p_fig4d <- (p_dendro / p_abund / p_meta_mna / p_meta_prog / p_meta_group) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 1, heights = panel_heights, guides = "collect")

p_fig4d

save_plot(p_fig4d, "Fig4d_combined_stacked.pdf", width = 8, height = 8.4)
```

## Patch detection

Subsequently, we detect tumor patches. We first detect connected sets of tumor cells with a predefined min. number of cells making up a patch and then we expand the concave hull around the patch by 1 pixel.

```{r patchDetection-1, fig.height=20, fig.width=20}
spe <- patchDetection(spe, 
                      patch_cells = spe$metacluster == "tumor",
                      img_id = "sample_id",
                      min_patch_size=20,
                      expand_by=1,
                      colPairName = "neighborhood")
```

### Distance to tumor-stroma border

Based on detected patches, the distance to the tumor stroma border can be computed. Therefore the [minDistToCells](https://bodenmillergroup.github.io/imcRtools/reference/minDistToCells.html) can be used. Negative values indicate cells within patches and positive values cells outside of patches.

```{r minDistCells}
spe <- minDistToCells(spe, 
                      x_cells = !is.na(spe$patch_id), 
                      img_id = "sample_id")

plotSpatial(spe[,spe$sample_id == "20220926_20220809_16-006_TU_003"], 
            node_color_by = "distToCells", 
            img_id = "sample_id", 
            node_size_fix = 0.5) +
    scale_color_gradient2(low = "dark blue", mid = "white", high = "dark red")
```

The distance distribution per celltype can be shown in ridge plots, with no
legend (the y-axis labels already name every group) so the ridges themselves
get the full plot width. We show this for both `celltype_2` (tumor celltypes +
non-tumor metaclusters) and the fine-grained `celltype`, and for each we mark
the core/border/stroma compartments (defined below using a 200 px threshold on
this same distance) in two ways: as translucent shaded background regions, or
as a green/red/blue compartment bar beneath a plain-background ridge plot. The
+/-200 px cutoff is also marked as dashed lines in every version.

```{r ridges-distance, fig.height=5,fig.width=8}
# Border threshold shown here matches `canonical_border` set in the
# spatial-compartments section below (kept as a literal since that section
# runs after this chunk).
border_threshold <- 200
x_range <- range(spe$distToCells, na.rm = TRUE)

# Compartment bar (green/red/blue core/border/stroma), shared by every "bar"
# distance-ridge figure below - only depends on border_threshold/x_range, not
# on the grouping variable.
compartment_bar <- ggplot() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = -border_threshold, ymin = 0, ymax = 1,
           fill = COL_COMPARTMENT[["core"]]) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -border_threshold, xmax = border_threshold, ymin = 0, ymax = 1,
           fill = COL_COMPARTMENT[["border"]]) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = border_threshold, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0, ymax = 1,
           fill = COL_COMPARTMENT[["stroma"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-border_threshold, border_threshold),
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = x_range, ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "distToCells") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank())

# Ridge plot (no legend - group names are the y-axis labels) for one grouping
# variable, in one of two compartment-display variants:
#  - "bar":    plain background, stacked on the shared compartment_bar below
#  - "shaded": core/border/stroma shown as translucent background regions
# Reused below for celltype_2, celltype, and cellular neighborhoods.
plot_dist_ridge <- function(group_var, y_label, fill_values, filename,
                            variant = c("bar", "shaded")) {
  variant <- match.arg(variant)

  dist_data <- as.data.frame(colData(spe)) %>%
    mutate(!!group_var := fct_reorder(.data[[group_var]], distToCells, .fun = median, .desc = TRUE))

  shaded_bg <- if (variant == "shaded") list(
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = -border_threshold, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = COL_COMPARTMENT[["core"]], alpha = 0.15),
    annotate("rect", xmin = -border_threshold, xmax = border_threshold, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = COL_COMPARTMENT[["border"]], alpha = 0.15),
    annotate("rect", xmin = border_threshold, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = COL_COMPARTMENT[["stroma"]], alpha = 0.15)
  ) else NULL

  p_ridge <- ggplot(dist_data) +
    shaded_bg +
    stat_density_ridges(aes(distToCells, .data[[group_var]], fill = .data[[group_var]]),
                        quantiles = c(0.5), quantile_lines = TRUE, scale = 3,
                        key_glyph = "rect") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "dark red", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-border_threshold, border_threshold),
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values) +
    labs(y = y_label) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = x_range, expand = FALSE) +
    theme_ridges() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  if (variant == "bar") {
    p_ridge <- p_ridge +
      theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
    p <- p_ridge / compartment_bar + plot_layout(heights = c(20, 1))
  } else {
    p <- p_ridge
  }

  save_plot(p, filename, width = 8, height = 5)
  p
}

# 1-2. celltype_2 (tumor celltypes + non-tumor metaclusters), bar and shaded
p_dist_celltype2_bar <- plot_dist_ridge(
  "celltype_2", "Celltype", metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_2,
  "Fig4j_border_distance_celltype2_bar.pdf", variant = "bar")
p_dist_celltype2_bar

p_dist_celltype2_shaded <- plot_dist_ridge(
  "celltype_2", "Celltype", metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_2,
  "Fig4j_border_distance_celltype2_shaded.pdf", variant = "shaded")
p_dist_celltype2_shaded

# 3-4. fine-grained celltype (all celltypes), bar and shaded
p_dist_celltype_bar <- plot_dist_ridge(
  "celltype", "Celltype (fine-grained)", metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype,
  "Fig4j_border_distance_celltype_bar.pdf", variant = "bar")
p_dist_celltype_bar

p_dist_celltype_shaded <- plot_dist_ridge(
  "celltype", "Celltype (fine-grained)", metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype,
  "Fig4j_border_distance_celltype_shaded.pdf", variant = "shaded")
p_dist_celltype_shaded
```

The same distance distribution, now grouped by cellular neighborhood (CN,
`cn_celltypes_2`, computed further below) instead of celltype.

```{r ridges-distance-neighborhood, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
p_dist_cn <- plot_dist_ridge("cn_celltypes_2", "Cellular neighborhood",
                             metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn,
                             "Fig4j_border_distance_neighborhood.pdf",
                             variant = "bar")

p_dist_cn
```

Based on the calculated distance for each cell, three compartments - tumor core, tumor/stroma border and stroma - can be defined using a distance threshold. We sweep border sizes from 100 to 300 pixels, visualizing the compartments and counting immune and tumor cells in each, and then adopt a border of 200 pixels for all downstream analyses. Image `20221018_20220906_03-018_TU_001` lacks tumor patches, therefore all cells are defined as `stroma` for this image.

```{r spatial-compartments}
thresholds        <- seq(100, 300, by = 50)
canonical_border  <- 200
no_patch_image    <- "20221018_20220906_03-018_TU_001"   # no tumor patches: all stroma
panel_sample_id_1 <- "20220926_20220809_16-006_TU_003"
# sanitize sample IDs for file-safe output tags
sanitize_sample_tag <- function(x) gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)
panel_sample_tag_1  <- sanitize_sample_tag(panel_sample_id_1)

# Compartment (core / border / stroma) for a given border size, as a plain
# vector (does not modify spe): border within `border` of the tumor-stroma
# interface, core further inside the tumor patches, stroma further outside.
compartment_at <- function(spe, border) {
  comp <- rep("stroma", ncol(spe))
  ok   <- spe$sample_id != no_patch_image
  comp[which(abs(spe$distToCells) <= border & ok)] <- "border"
  comp[which(comp != "border" & spe$distToCells <= border & ok)] <- "core"
  comp
}

plot_list_img1 <- list()
results_list   <- list()

for (th in thresholds) {
  spe$compartment <- compartment_at(spe, th)

  # per-threshold compartment map for the panel sample
  p_s2 <- plotSpatial(
    spe[, spe$sample_id == panel_sample_id_1],
    node_color_by = "compartment",
    img_id = "sample_id",
    node_size_fix = 0.5
  ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = COL_COMPARTMENT) +
    ggtitle(paste("Border size =", th))

  save_plot(
    p_s2,
    paste0("Fig4g3_tumor_patch_", th, ".pdf"),
    width = 6,
    height = 6
  )

  plot_list_img1[[as.character(th)]] <- p_s2

  # immune and tumor counts per compartment
  results_list[[as.character(th)]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(table(compartment = spe$compartment[spe$celltype_3 == "immune"]), cell_class = "immune"),
    data.frame(table(compartment = spe$compartment[spe$metacluster == "tumor"]),  cell_class = "tumor")
  ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(count = Freq) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(threshold = th)
}

# Canonical compartment definition (border = 200) used by all downstream
# analyses; the loop above leaves spe$compartment at its last threshold (300).
spe$compartment <- compartment_at(spe, canonical_border)

results_df <- bind_rows(results_list) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = c("core", "border", "stroma")),
                cell_class  = factor(cell_class, levels = c("immune", "tumor")))

panel_img1 <- wrap_plots(plot_list_img1, ncol = length(thresholds)) +
  plot_annotation(title = panel_sample_id_1)

save_plot(
  panel_img1,
  paste0("Fig4g3_tumor_patch_panel_all_thresholds_", panel_sample_tag_1, ".pdf"),
  width = 30,
  height = 6
)

panel_img1

# cell counts by compartment, per border size
y_axis_upper_expand <- 0.1
plot_bordersize_counts <- function(df, title) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = factor(threshold), y = count, fill = compartment)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
    geom_text(aes(label = count), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.25, size = 3) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Border size", y = "Cell count") +
    theme_classic() +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, y_axis_upper_expand)))
}

immune_plot <- plot_bordersize_counts(results_df %>% filter(cell_class == "immune"),
                                      "Immune cell counts by compartment")
save_plot(immune_plot, "Fig4g3_tumor_bordersize_immune_barplot.pdf", width = 6, height = 6)
immune_plot

tumor_plot <- plot_bordersize_counts(results_df %>% filter(cell_class == "tumor"),
                                     "Tumor cell counts by compartment")
save_plot(tumor_plot, "Fig4g3_tumor_bordersize_tumor_barplot.pdf", width = 6, height = 6)
tumor_plot

# combined immune + tumor barplot (one facet each)
immune_tumor_plot <- plot_bordersize_counts(results_df, "Immune and tumor cell counts by compartment") +
  facet_wrap(~cell_class, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y")
save_plot(immune_tumor_plot, "Fig4g3_tumor_bordersize_immune_tumor_barplot.pdf", width = 6, height = 10)
```

### DA analysis in spatial compartments

Next, we will plot the differential abundance of cell types with respect to spatial compartment on a sample level. We analyse tumor celltypes, immune metaclusters, and cellular neighborhoods, looping over all three compartment comparison pairs (`core-border`, `core-stroma`, `border-stroma`). Differential abundance is tested with `diffcyt` (`testDA_edgeR`) controlling for sample-level pairing, and shown as paired boxplots (point size = number of cells, lines connecting the same sample).

```{r define-markers}

# Define cell_type_markers
type_markers <- c("MPO_Y89_mean", "CD44_In115_mean", "CD11b_Nd142_mean", "HLA-DR_Nd143_mean", "PRPH_Nd144_mean", "HLA-ABC_Sm147_mean", "CD20_Nd148_mean", "LUM_Sm149_mean", "CD11c_Nd150_mean",
                  "CD24_Eu151_mean", "CD3_Sm152_mean", "CD45_Eu153_mean", "CD8a_Sm154_mean", "GD2_Gd155_mean", "CD34_Gd156_mean", "CD10_Gd158_mean", "CXCR4_Tb159_mean","SOX10_Dy162_mean",
                  "FOXP3_Dy163_mean", "CHGA_Dy164_mean", "GATA3_Er168_mean", "CD56_Er170_mean", "CD4_Yb171_mean", "ELAVL4_Yb174_mean", "CD14_Lu175_mean", "Vimentin_Pt196_mean", "CD15_Bi209_mean")

# Define cell_state_markers
state_markers <- c("CD274_Gd160_mean", "S100B_Dy161_mean", "CD279_Ho165_mean", "Ki-67_Tm169_mean", "GZMB_Yb173_mean")

```

```{r cluster-order-colors}
# Cluster display orders used throughout the compartment analyses (immune_order
# are metacluster names; tumor_order are current spe$celltype_2 names;
# neighborhood_order are the cn_celltypes_2 cluster numbers, as characters).
immune_order <- c("T cells", "B cells", "myeloid/NK", "granulocytes")

tumor_order <- c("adrenergic marker-low Tu", "GD2neg Tu", "CD44+ Tu", "Ki67+ Tu",
                 "neuroblast-like Tu", "early neuroblast-like Tu")
# keep only the celltypes actually present in the data (preserves order)
tumor_order <- intersect(tumor_order,
                         unique(as.character(spe$celltype_2[spe$metacluster == "tumor"])))

neighborhood_order <- levels(spe$cn_celltypes_2)

# Remaining non-tumor, non-immune metaclusters (mesenchymal, other), used to
# pad the pooled "tumor_immune" stacked bar to all cells (so its n= total
# matches the "neighborhood" stacked bar, which counts every cell).
other_order <- intersect(c("mesenchymal", "other"), unique(as.character(spe$celltype_2)))

# Color lookup, falling back to grey if a cluster has no (or NA) color. Looks
# up col_celltype_2 by default; pass color_vec = col_cn for neighborhoods.
cluster_color <- function(name, color_vec = metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_2) {
  col <- unname(color_vec[as.character(name)])
  if (length(col) == 0 || is.na(col)) "grey50" else col
}

cells_list       <- c("tumor", "immune", "neighborhood")
comp_levels      <- c("core", "border", "stroma")
comparison_pairs <- list(c("core","border"), c("core","stroma"), c("border","stroma"))

# Cells, cluster column, display order and colors of each cell class: celltype_2
# for tumor / immune / tumor_immune (all celltypes pooled, stacked bars only);
# cn_celltypes_2 for neighborhoods, so every cell counts.
class_definition <- function(cells) {
  list(
    order         = switch(cells,
                           immune       = immune_order,
                           tumor        = tumor_order,
                           neighborhood = neighborhood_order,
                           tumor_immune = c(tumor_order, immune_order, other_order)),
    keep          = switch(cells,
                           immune       = spe$metacluster %in% immune_order,
                           tumor        = spe$metacluster == "tumor",
                           neighborhood = rep(TRUE, ncol(spe)),
                           tumor_immune = spe$metacluster %in% c("tumor", immune_order, other_order)),
    cluster_field = if (cells == "neighborhood") "cn_celltypes_2" else "celltype_2",
    color_vec     = if (cells == "neighborhood") metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_cn else
                                                 metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_2
  )
}
```

Cells of each cluster per sample (`fm_id`) and compartment, with zero counts
kept (e.g. samples without a core). These counts are the basis of the
proportions below, of the cell-count tables and of the densities.

```{r compartment-counts}
sample_levels  <- sort(unique(spe$fm_id))
patient_lookup <- dplyr::distinct(data.frame(fm_id = spe$fm_id, patient_id = spe$patient_id))

count_cells <- function(cells) {
  def <- class_definition(cells)
  data.frame(
    fm_id       = factor(spe$fm_id, levels = sample_levels),
    compartment = factor(spe$compartment, levels = comp_levels),
    cluster_id  = factor(spe[[def$cluster_field]], levels = def$order)
  )[def$keep, ] %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(compartment), !is.na(cluster_id)) %>%
    dplyr::count(fm_id, compartment, cluster_id, name = "n", .drop = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(cells = cells)
}

# n = cells of the cluster, total = cells of the class, Freq = % of the class
# (NaN for an empty compartment)
counts_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(cells_list, count_cells)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(fm_id = as.character(fm_id)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(patient_lookup, by = "fm_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cells = factor(cells, levels = cells_list)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cells, fm_id, compartment) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(total = sum(n), Freq = 100 * n / total) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r compartment-da}
keep_rows <- rowData(spe)$use_channel

# helper to build marker_info from the global marker vectors
.make_marker_info <- function(spe, keep_rows) {
  channel_name <- sapply(strsplit(rownames(rowData(spe)[keep_rows, ]), "_"), "[[", 2)
  marker_name  <- sapply(strsplit(rownames(rowData(spe)[keep_rows, ]), "_"), "[[", 1)
  marker_class <- ifelse(rownames(rowData(spe)[keep_rows, ]) %in% type_markers, "type",
                  ifelse(rownames(rowData(spe)[keep_rows, ]) %in% state_markers, "state", "other"))
  data.frame(channel_name, marker_name,
             marker_class = factor(marker_class),
             row.names = marker_name)
}

marker_info_da <- .make_marker_info(spe, keep_rows)

# "log2FC (adj. p stars)" label for the boxplot brackets (also used for the
# density tests below)
stat_label <- function(logFC, p_adj) {
  stars <- dplyr::if_else(is.na(p_adj), "NA", trimws(gtools::stars.pval(p_adj)))
  stars <- dplyr::if_else(stars == "", "ns", stars)
  paste0(round(logFC, 2), " (", dplyr::if_else(is.na(p_adj), "NA", sprintf("%.3f", p_adj)), " ", stars, ")")
}

# diffcyt (testDA_edgeR) for the cells `keep_cols` of one cell class in the two
# compartments `comps`, paired by sample; NULL if the test fails
diffcyt_pair <- function(keep_cols, comps, def) {
  sce_da <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(
      counts = assay(spe, "counts")[keep_rows, keep_cols],
      exprs  = assay(spe, "counts")[keep_rows, keep_cols]
    )
  )
  sce_da$fm_id       <- spe[keep_rows, keep_cols]$fm_id
  sce_da$sample      <- factor(spe[keep_rows, keep_cols]$sample)
  sce_da$compartment <- factor(spe[keep_rows, keep_cols]$compartment, levels = comps)
  sce_da$sample_id   <- factor(paste0(sce_da$fm_id, "_", sce_da$compartment))
  sce_da$condition   <- factor(sce_da$compartment, levels = comps)
  sce_da$cluster_id  <- factor(spe[keep_rows, keep_cols][[def$cluster_field]], levels = def$order)

  metadata(sce_da)$cluster_codes   <- data.frame(celltype = sce_da$cluster_id)
  metadata(sce_da)$experiment_info <- as.data.frame(colData(sce_da)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(sample_id, condition, sample) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(n_cells = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    as.data.frame()

  exp_info           <- metadata(sce_da)$experiment_info
  exp_info           <- exp_info[match(unique(sce_da$sample_id), exp_info$sample_id), ]
  exp_info$condition <- factor(exp_info$condition, levels = comps)

  df_list_da <- lapply(unique(sce_da$sample_id), function(x)
    as.data.frame(t(counts(sce_da[, sce_da$sample_id == x]))))
  names(df_list_da) <- unique(sce_da$sample_id)

  d_se_da <- prepareData(df_list_da, exp_info, marker_info_da)
  rowData(d_se_da)$cluster_id     <- sce_da[, rownames(d_se_da)]$cluster_id
  metadata(d_se_da)$cluster_codes <- metadata(sce_da)$cluster_codes
  d_se_da     <- transformData(d_se_da)
  d_counts_da <- calcCounts(d_se_da)

  design_da   <- createDesignMatrix(exp_info, cols_design = c("condition", "sample"))
  contrast_da <- createContrast(c(0, 1, rep(0, length(unique(exp_info$sample)) - 1)))

  res_DA_da <- tryCatch(
    testDA_edgeR(d_counts_da, design_da, contrast_da,
                 min_cells = 3,
                 min_samples = round(ncol(d_counts_da) * 0.2)),
    error = function(e) { message("diffcyt failed for ", paste(comps, collapse = "-"), ": ", e$message); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(res_DA_da)) NULL else data.frame(rowData(res_DA_da))
}

# diffcyt stats of one cell class for every compartment pair
run_compartment_da <- function(cells) {
  def <- class_definition(cells)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(comparison_pairs, function(comps) {
    keep_cols <- def$keep & spe$compartment %in% comps
    res       <- if (sum(keep_cols) >= 10) diffcyt_pair(keep_cols, comps, def)

    # samples with cells in both compartments (the ones informative for the pairing)
    pair_totals <- table(spe$fm_id[keep_cols], factor(spe$compartment[keep_cols], levels = comps))

    data.frame(cluster_name = def$order,
               group1       = comps[1],
               group2       = comps[2],
               n_samples    = sum(apply(pair_totals > 0, 1, all)),
               p_adj        = if (is.null(res)) NA_real_ else res[def$order, "p_adj"],
               logFC        = if (is.null(res)) NA_real_ else round(res[def$order, "logFC"], 2))
  })) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(label = stat_label(logFC, p_adj))
}

da_stats <- lapply(setNames(cells_list, cells_list), run_compartment_da)

for (cells in cells_list) {
  save_table(da_stats[[cells]], paste0("compartment_DA_stats_", cells, ".csv"),
             if (cells == "neighborhood") "neighborhood_level" else "celltype_level")
  print(knitr::kable(da_stats[[cells]], caption = cells))
}
```

Each point is sized by the number of cells of the class in that sample and
compartment (the denominator of the proportion), and the points of one sample
are connected across core / border / stroma.

```{r compartment-boxplots-paired}
max_plot_columns <- 5

# Paired boxplot of one cluster across compartments: one line per sample, point
# size = the denominator (`size`: cells of the class, or compartment area).
# Percentages get a fixed 0-100 axis with the pairwise brackets drawn above it
# (clip = "off"); densities a free axis with headroom for the brackets.
plot_paired <- function(df, y, size, stats_df, cluster_name, color_cluster,
                        size_limits, size_name, y_label, percent) {
  y_top <- if (percent) 100 else max(df[[y]], 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  stats_df$y.position <- y_top * (1.06 + 0.14 * (seq_len(nrow(stats_df)) - 1))

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = compartment, y = .data[[y]])) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = color_cluster, color = "black", outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
    geom_line(aes(group = fm_id), color = "grey40", alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(size = .data[[size]]), color = "black") +
    stat_pvalue_manual(stats_df, y.position = "y.position", label = "label") +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = comp_levels) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 5, limits = size_limits, name = size_name) +
    ggtitle(str_wrap(cluster_name, width = 18)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = y_label) +
    theme_pubr() +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1.0, legend.position = "right",
          plot.title  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14,
                                     margin = margin(b = if (percent) 85 else 12)),
          plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 8, b = 8, l = 8))

  if (percent)
    p + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0))) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100), clip = "off")
  else
    p + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))) +
      coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
}

# One paired boxplot per cluster of a cell class, with one shared size legend
plot_paired_panels <- function(cells, df, stats, y, size, size_name, y_label, percent) {
  def         <- class_definition(cells)
  size_limits <- c(0, max(df[[size]], na.rm = TRUE))
  panels <- lapply(def$order, function(cluster_name)
    plot_paired(dplyr::filter(df, cluster_id == cluster_name), y, size,
                dplyr::filter(stats, cluster_name == !!cluster_name), cluster_name,
                cluster_color(cluster_name, def$color_vec), size_limits, size_name, y_label, percent))

  n_cols <- min(length(panels), max_plot_columns)
  list(plot   = wrap_plots(panels, ncol = n_cols) + plot_layout(guides = "collect"),
       width  = 3 * n_cols + 2,
       height = 4.5 * ceiling(length(panels) / n_cols))
}

for (cells in cells_list) {
  panels <- plot_paired_panels(
    cells, dplyr::filter(counts_long, cells == !!cells, total > 0), da_stats[[cells]],
    y = "Freq", size = "total", size_name = "cells in\ncompartment",
    y_label = if (cells == "neighborhood") "% of all cells" else paste0("% of ", cells, " cells"),
    percent = TRUE)

  save_plot(panels$plot, paste0("Fig4m_boxplot_compartments_", cells, ".pdf"),
            width = panels$width, height = panels$height)
  print(panels$plot)
}
```

Finally, we summarize the cell-type composition of each compartment as stacked bars, drawn for every border size and shown for immune metaclusters, tumor celltypes, all celltypes pooled together (tumor + immune + mesenchymal + other, so its total matches the neighborhood bar below), and cellular neighborhoods.

```{r composition-stacked-bars}
# spe$compartment (the canonical-border assignment) is left untouched;
# each border's compartment is computed on the fly with compartment_at().

# One stacked-bar figure for a compartment vector and a cell class (see
# class_definition(); "tumor_immune" = all celltypes pooled).
make_compartment_stackedbar <- function(comp_vec, cells, border) {
  def <- class_definition(cells)

  df_bar <- data.frame(compartment = comp_vec, cluster_id = spe[[def$cluster_field]])
  df_bar <- df_bar[def$keep & df_bar$compartment %in% comp_levels, ]

  totals <- df_bar %>% dplyr::group_by(compartment) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(N = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  df_prop <- df_bar %>%
    dplyr::group_by(compartment, cluster_id) %>% dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(compartment) %>% dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = comp_levels),
                  cluster_id  = factor(cluster_id,  levels = def$order))

  color_vec <- def$color_vec[def$order]
  lab       <- if (cells == "tumor_immune") "all celltypes" else cells

  p_stack <- ggplot(df_prop, aes(x = compartment, y = pct, fill = cluster_id)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(
      data = totals %>% dplyr::mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = comp_levels)),
      aes(x = compartment, y = 103, label = paste0("n=", N)),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 0, size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = color_vec, drop = FALSE, name = "Cell type") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 115), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    labs(title = paste0("Compartment composition (", lab, ") - border ", border),
         x = "Compartment", y = "% cells") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"))

  save_plot(p_stack,
            paste0("Fig4_suppl_stackedbar_compartments_", cells, "_bordersize_", border, ".pdf"),
            width = if (cells == "tumor_immune") 7 else 6, height = 5)
  print(p_stack)
}

for (border in thresholds) {
  comp_vec <- compartment_at(spe, border)
  for (cells in c("immune", "tumor", "tumor_immune", "neighborhood"))
    make_compartment_stackedbar(comp_vec, cells, border)
}
```



## Cells per sample and compartment

Cell counts per sample (`fm_id`) and compartment (outputs in `cell_counts`).

### Samples, images and patients

The compartment statistics pool all images of a sample (`fm_id`), while the
`diffcyt` design uses the `sample` column (image name without the image number,
which also carries the acquisition date). Both should map one-to-one; samples
where they do not are listed below.

```{r sample-overview}
cell_df <- data.frame(
  patient_id  = spe$patient_id,
  fm_id       = spe$fm_id,
  sample      = spe$sample,
  sample_id   = spe$sample_id,
  compartment = spe$compartment,
  metacluster = spe$metacluster
)

sample_overview <- cell_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(patient_id, fm_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_images  = dplyr::n_distinct(sample_id),
                   n_sample  = dplyr::n_distinct(sample),
                   n_cells   = dplyr::n(),
                   .groups   = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(patient_id, fm_id)

save_table(sample_overview, "sample_overview.csv", "cell_counts")
knitr::kable(sample_overview)

# fm_ids whose images carry several `sample` values (would break the diffcyt pairing)
sample_overview %>% dplyr::filter(n_sample > 1)

# patients with more than one PT sample
sample_overview %>% dplyr::count(patient_id) %>% dplyr::filter(n > 1)
```

### Cells per cell type

Cell counts per sample (`fm_id`) and compartment (`counts_long`, see above),
per cluster and as totals per cell class (the denominators of the proportions).
Zero counts are kept explicitly (e.g. samples without a core).

How many samples would be kept at a given minimum number of cells: per
compartment, and per compartment pair (a sample enters a paired comparison only
if both compartments reach the threshold).

```{r cell-count-thresholds}
samples_per_compartment <- totals %>%
  tidyr::crossing(min_cells = count_thresholds) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cells, min_cells, compartment) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_samples = sum(total >= min_cells), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = n_samples)

samples_per_pair <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(comparison_pairs, function(pair) {
  totals %>%
    dplyr::filter(compartment %in% pair) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(cells, fm_id) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(pair_min = min(total), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::crossing(min_cells = count_thresholds) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(cells, min_cells) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(n_samples = sum(pair_min >= min_cells), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pair = paste(pair, collapse = "-"))
})) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = pair, values_from = n_samples)

samples_kept <- dplyr::left_join(samples_per_compartment, samples_per_pair,
                                 by = c("cells", "min_cells"))
save_table(samples_kept, "samples_kept_per_min_cells.csv", "cell_counts")
knitr::kable(samples_kept, caption = paste0("Samples with at least min_cells cells (of ",
                                            length(sample_levels), " samples)"))
```

## Density analysis

Cells per mm² of compartment, from compartment areas defined around the cells
(outputs in `density_analysis`).

### Compartment areas

To turn counts into densities (cells per mm²), we need the area of each
compartment per image (1 px = 1 µm). Two rules:

1. tissue: there is no tissue mask, so only area within a tissue radius of a
   cell centre counts; larger empty regions are excluded. The image extent is
   the bounding box of the cell centres. Areas (and the densities below) are
   computed for tissue radii of 50, 75 and 100 µm, with the outputs of each
   radius in its own `density_analysis/tissue_radius_<r>um` subfolder;
2. each piece of tissue takes the compartment (core / border / stroma,
   `spe$compartment`) of its nearest cell, i.e. the Voronoi tiles of the cells,
   merged per compartment.

By construction every cell lies inside its own compartment (checked per image),
and core and stroma can only touch across an empty gap, which the tissue mask
removes (the core-stroma contact is reported and should be 0).

```{r compartment-area-params}
tissue_radii       <- c(50, 75, 100)   # um; area further than this from any cell is empty (no tissue)
tissue_radius_main <- 50               # um; radius whose density plots are shown in this report
example_images     <- c("20220926_20220809_16-006_TU_003",
                        "20220925_20220804_17-001_TU_002")
```

```{r compartment-areas}
# Assign points to the compartment polygons
classify_by_polygon <- function(points, regions) {
  comp <- rep("stroma", nrow(points))
  pts  <- st_cast(st_sfc(st_multipoint(points)), "POINT")
  comp[lengths(st_intersects(pts, regions$border)) > 0] <- "border"
  comp[lengths(st_intersects(pts, regions$core))   > 0] <- "core"
  comp
}

cell_coords <- spatialCoords(spe)[, c("Pos_X", "Pos_Y")]

area_results <- lapply(unique(spe$sample_id), function(img) {
  sel       <- spe$sample_id == img
  cell_xy   <- cell_coords[sel, , drop = FALSE]
  cell_comp <- spe$compartment[sel]

  # image extent = bounding box of the cell centres
  x_range <- range(cell_xy[, 1])
  y_range <- range(cell_xy[, 2])
  roi <- st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(c(x_range[1], y_range[1]), c(x_range[2], y_range[1]),
                                      c(x_range[2], y_range[2]), c(x_range[1], y_range[2]),
                                      c(x_range[1], y_range[1])))))

  cells_sfc <- st_cast(st_sfc(st_multipoint(cell_xy)), "POINT")
  empty     <- st_sfc(st_polygon())

  # rule 2 (independent of the tissue radius): Voronoi tile of every cell,
  # labelled with its cell's compartment and merged per compartment
  tiles     <- st_collection_extract(st_voronoi(st_sfc(st_multipoint(cell_xy)), envelope = roi), "POLYGON")
  tile_cell <- sapply(st_intersects(tiles, cells_sfc), `[`, 1)   # cell generating each tile
  comp_area <- lapply(setNames(comp_levels, comp_levels), function(comp) {
    in_comp <- which(cell_comp[tile_cell] == comp)
    if (length(in_comp) == 0) empty else st_intersection(st_union(tiles[in_comp]), roi)
  })

  lapply(setNames(tissue_radii, tissue_radii), function(r) {
    # rule 1: tissue = area within r of a cell centre
    tissue  <- st_intersection(st_union(st_buffer(cells_sfc, r, nQuadSegs = 4)), roi)
    regions <- lapply(comp_area, function(g) {
      g <- st_intersection(g, tissue)
      if (length(g) == 0) empty else g
    })

    # core and stroma should never share a boundary (length in px)
    core_stroma_contact <- tryCatch(
      sum(st_length(st_collection_extract(st_intersection(regions$core, regions$stroma), "LINESTRING"))),
      error = function(e) NA_real_)

    cell_poly <- classify_by_polygon(cell_xy, regions)

    list(
      areas     = data.frame(sample_id     = img,
                             tissue_radius = r,
                             compartment   = comp_levels,
                             area_mm2      = sapply(regions[comp_levels], function(g) sum(st_area(g))) / 1e6),
      roi       = data.frame(sample_id           = img,
                             tissue_radius       = r,
                             width_px            = diff(x_range),
                             height_px           = diff(y_range),
                             tissue_fraction     = sum(st_area(tissue)) / sum(st_area(roi)),
                             core_stroma_contact = core_stroma_contact,
                             n_cells             = sum(sel),
                             agreement           = mean(cell_poly == cell_comp)),
      confusion = data.frame(sample_id = img,
                             cell_rule = cell_comp,
                             polygon   = cell_poly) %>%
                    dplyr::count(sample_id, cell_rule, polygon) %>%
                    dplyr::mutate(tissue_radius = r),
      example   = if (img %in% example_images) regions
    )
  })
})
names(area_results) <- unique(spe$sample_id)

# collect one part of the results over all images and radii
collect_area_results <- function(part)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(area_results, function(x) dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(x, `[[`, part))))

# subfolder per tissue radius
radius_dir <- function(base, r) file.path(base, paste0("tissue_radius_", r, "um"))

# 1. per image: extent, share counted as tissue, core-stroma contact (should
# be 0), and share of cells inside the polygon of their own compartment
roi_table      <- collect_area_results("roi")
area_confusion <- collect_area_results("confusion")

# 2. areas per image and per sample (all images of a sample summed)
areas_image_all <- collect_area_results("areas") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(cell_df, sample_id, fm_id, patient_id), by = "sample_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = comp_levels))

areas_sample_all <- areas_image_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tissue_radius, patient_id, fm_id, compartment) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(area_mm2 = sum(area_mm2), .groups = "drop")

for (r in tissue_radii) {
  sub <- radius_dir("density_analysis", r)
  save_table(dplyr::filter(roi_table, tissue_radius == r), "compartment_area_image_qc.csv", sub)
  save_table(dplyr::filter(area_confusion, tissue_radius == r), "compartment_area_polygon_confusion.csv", sub)
  save_table(areas_image_all %>% dplyr::filter(tissue_radius == r) %>%
               tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = area_mm2),
             "compartment_area_per_image_mm2.csv", sub)
  save_table(areas_sample_all %>% dplyr::filter(tissue_radius == r) %>%
               tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = area_mm2),
             "compartment_area_per_sample_mm2.csv", sub)
}

             tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(compartment, tissue_radius), values_from = area_mm2,
                                names_glue = "{compartment}_{tissue_radius}um"),
           "compartment_area_per_sample_all_radii_mm2.csv", "density_analysis")

roi_table %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tissue_radius) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(median_tissue_fraction  = median(tissue_fraction),
                   min_tissue_fraction     = min(tissue_fraction),
                   median_agreement        = median(agreement),
                   min_agreement           = min(agreement),
                   max_core_stroma_contact = max(core_stroma_contact, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Per tissue radius: share of the image counted as tissue, share of cells inside their compartment polygon, core-stroma contact (px)")

areas_sample_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tissue_radius, compartment) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(total_area_mm2 = sum(area_mm2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = compartment, values_from = total_area_mm2) %>%
```

```{r compartment-area-plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
p_radius <- ggplot(areas_sample_all, aes(x = tissue_radius, y = area_mm2, group = fm_id)) +

  facet_wrap(~ compartment, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = tissue_radii) +
  labs(x = "tissue_radius (um)", y = expression("area (mm"^2*")"),
       title = "Compartment area per sample vs. tissue radius") +
  theme_pubr()

save_plot(p_radius, "compartment_area_vs_tissue_radius.pdf", subdir = "density_analysis", width = 10, height = 4)
p_radius
```

### Densities per compartment

Cells per mm² of compartment, per sample (all images summed), for each tissue
radius (outputs in `density_analysis/tissue_radius_<r>um`, and which calls
depend on the radius in `density_analysis/`). For each cluster
and compartment pair, densities are compared with a negative-binomial GLM on
the counts with the compartment area as offset and the sample as a fixed effect
(the same paired design as the `diffcyt` test, `~ condition + sample`), fitted
per cluster with `MASS::glm.nb`. Samples with an empty compartment (area 0) or
with no cells of the cluster in either compartment are left out of that test.
The log2 fold change is the second compartment of the pair vs. the first (as
in `diffcyt`), and p-values are BH-adjusted across clusters within each cell
class and compartment pair.

```{r densities}
# densities for every tissue radius
density_df_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(tissue_radii, function(r) {
  counts_long %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("sample_label")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(areas_sample_all %>%
                       dplyr::filter(tissue_radius == r) %>%
                       dplyr::select(fm_id, compartment, area_mm2),
                     by = c("fm_id", "compartment")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(tissue_radius = r,
                  area_mm2      = dplyr::coalesce(area_mm2, 0),
                  density       = dplyr::if_else(area_mm2 > 0, n / area_mm2, NA_real_))
}))

for (r in tissue_radii) {
  for (cells in cells_list) {
    save_table(density_df_all %>%
                 dplyr::filter(tissue_radius == r, cells == !!cells) %>%
                 dplyr::select(patient_id, fm_id, compartment, area_mm2, cluster_id, density) %>%
                 tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cluster_id, values_from = density) %>%
                 dplyr::arrange(patient_id, fm_id, compartment),
               paste0("density_per_sample_compartment_", cells, ".csv"), radius_dir("density_analysis", r))
  }
}

# NB GLM for one cluster and compartment pair
test_density_pair <- function(df, pair) {
  d <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(compartment %in% pair, area_mm2 > 0) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(fm_id) %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() == 2, sum(n) > 0) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(compartment = factor(as.character(compartment), levels = pair),
                  fm_id       = factor(fm_id))

  if (dplyr::n_distinct(d$fm_id) < 3) return(data.frame(n_samples = dplyr::n_distinct(d$fm_id), logFC = NA_real_, p_val = NA_real_))

  fit <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(MASS::glm.nb(n ~ compartment + fm_id + offset(log(area_mm2)), data = d)),
    error = function(e) { message("glm.nb failed: ", e$message); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(fit)) return(data.frame(n_samples = dplyr::n_distinct(d$fm_id), logFC = NA_real_, p_val = NA_real_))

  coefs    <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  coef_row <- if (paste0("compartment", pair[2]) %in% rownames(coefs))
                coefs[paste0("compartment", pair[2]), ] else
                c(Estimate = NA_real_, `Pr(>|z|)` = NA_real_)
  data.frame(n_samples = dplyr::n_distinct(d$fm_id),
             logFC     = unname(coef_row["Estimate"]) / log(2),
             p_val     = unname(coef_row["Pr(>|z|)"]))
}

# All clusters of a cell class, all compartment pairs (BH within class x pair)
density_tests <- function(cells, dens) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(comparison_pairs, function(pair) {
    res <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(class_definition(cells)$order, function(cluster_name) {
      cluster_df <- dplyr::filter(dens, cells == !!cells, cluster_id == cluster_name)
      data.frame(cluster_name = cluster_name, test_density_pair(cluster_df, pair))
    }))
    res$p_adj  <- p.adjust(res$p_val, method = "BH")
    res$cells  <- cells
    res$group1 <- pair[1]
    res$group2 <- pair[2]
    res
  }))
}

density_stats_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(tissue_radii, function(r) {
  dens_r <- dplyr::filter(density_df_all, tissue_radius == r)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(cells_list, density_tests, dens = dens_r)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(tissue_radius = r)
})) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = stat_label(logFC, p_adj))

for (r in tissue_radii)
  save_table(dplyr::filter(density_stats_all, tissue_radius == r),
             "density_compartment_stats.csv", radius_dir("density_analysis", r))

# does a call (up / down at adj. p < 0.05, or ns) depend on the tissue radius?
density_radius_check <- density_stats_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pair = paste(group1, group2, sep = "-"),
                call = dplyr::case_when(is.na(p_adj) ~ "NA",
                                        p_adj >= 0.05 ~ "ns",
                                        logFC > 0     ~ "up",
                                        TRUE          ~ "down")) %>%
  dplyr::select(cells, cluster_name, pair, tissue_radius, logFC, p_adj, call) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cells, cluster_name, pair) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(changed = dplyr::n_distinct(call) > 1) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tissue_radius, values_from = c(logFC, p_adj, call),
                     names_glue = "{.value}_{tissue_radius}um")

save_table(density_radius_check, "density_calls_per_tissue_radius.csv", "density_analysis")
cat(sum(density_radius_check$changed), "of", nrow(density_radius_check),
    "density tests change their call between tissue radii", paste(tissue_radii, collapse = " / "), "um\n")
knitr::kable(dplyr::filter(density_radius_check, changed), digits = 3,
             caption = "Density tests whose call depends on the tissue radius")
```

Paired density boxplots, as above: one line per sample, point size = area of
the compartment (the denominator of the density), one set per tissue radius.

```{r density-boxplots}
for (r in tissue_radii) {
  for (cells in cells_list) {
    panels <- plot_paired_panels(
      cells,
      dplyr::filter(density_df_all, tissue_radius == r, cells == !!cells, !is.na(density)),
      dplyr::filter(density_stats_all, tissue_radius == r, cells == !!cells),
      y = "density", size = "area_mm2",
      size_name = expression(atop("compartment", "area (mm"^2*")")),
      y_label = expression("cells / mm"^2), percent = FALSE)
    p_density <- panels$plot + plot_annotation(title = paste0("tissue_radius = ", r, " um"))

    save_plot(p_density, paste0("Fig4m_density_compartments_paired_", cells, ".pdf"),
              subdir = radius_dir("density_analysis", r),
              width = panels$width, height = panels$height + 0.5)
    if (r == tissue_radius_main) print(p_density)
  }
}
```
